name: Brotli
summary: Current upstream Google Brotli 1.2.0 CLI compiled for browser WebAssembly from the exact official tag/commit without source patches.

profiles.label: Browser Full
profiles.output: Generic upstream brotli CLI; input and output files are staged in browser MEMFS
profiles.size: Loaded from the published release manifest

capabilityMatrix.note: The feasibility build links the upstream c/tools/brotli.c target through the upstream CMake project; no replacement compressor CLI is introduced.
The browser smoke performs a real quality-11 compression, integrity check and decompression round trip.
Browser execution uses Emscripten MEMFS, so host ownership/permission/time metadata semantics are not exposed as native filesystem behavior.
The first feasibility profile is single-threaded and does not require cross-origin isolation.

comparison.name: Upstream native
comparison.note: Official Google Brotli C libraries and brotli CLI on the host filesystem.

comparison.name: WASM Zoo
comparison.note: Same reviewed upstream tag/commit and upstream CMake brotli CLI target compiled with Emscripten; filesystem I/O is isolated to MEMFS.

notes: Brotli 1.2.0 is built from the exact upstream v1.2.0 tag at commit 028fb5a23661f123017c060daa546b55cf4bde29 using the upstream CMake brotli executable target.
The reviewed browser-full build preserves the upstream CLI and has zero Brotli source patches; the browser-specific boundary is limited to Worker execution and Emscripten MEMFS file staging.

The initial package release is brotli-v0.1.0. A human maintainer creates the reviewed package tag; the tag-triggered workflow rebuilds, smoke-tests and publishes immutable binary/source/checksum/provenance/SBOM assets.

Stable Google Brotli GitHub Releases are eligible for exact-tag/commit browser-full candidate builds and review-only promotion PRs. Automation may prepare the reviewed pin change after the real Chromium gate passes, but merge, package tag, GitHub Release and any future npm publication remain human-controlled.

@wasm-zoo/brotli@0.1.0 is in prepublication canary review from the immutable brotli-v0.1.0 / browser-full Release asset. The canary tarball must pass real Vite Chromium, Firefox and WebKit CLI operations before any first Registry publication; canary metadata alone does not enroll Brotli in the Registry-backed Cross-browser Lab.

integration.summary: Self-host browser-brotli.js, wasm-zoo.mjs and the reviewed Brotli core files, stage input/output files in MEMFS, then execute ordinary upstream brotli CLI arguments locally in a Worker.
integration.example:
<script src="/vendor/brotli/browser-brotli.js"></script>
<script>
const brotli = WasmZooBrotli.loadHosted({ baseUrl: "/vendor/brotli/" });
await brotli.load();
const result = await brotli.exec(["-q", "11", "-o", "/output.br", "/input.bin"], {
  files: [{ name: "/input.bin", data: inputBytes }],
  outputs: ["/output.br"]
});
console.log(result.files[0].data);
brotli.dispose();
</script>
notes: No SharedArrayBuffer or cross-origin isolation is required for browser-full.
The wrapper preserves the upstream CLI argument model and adds only Worker isolation, MEMFS staging and stdout/stderr capture.
Native host filesystem metadata semantics are not available; files must be staged explicitly into MEMFS.

docs.description: Unofficial WASM Zoo distribution of the upstream Google Brotli 1.2.0 CLI for browsers.
docs.runtimeNote: Single-threaded upstream brotli CLI in an isolated Web Worker with Emscripten MEMFS. No SharedArrayBuffer or cross-origin isolation is required. Inputs and outputs are explicitly staged in browser memory; the package preserves ordinary upstream CLI arguments rather than replacing Brotli with a JavaScript codec API.
